primary_source.headline: Power supply hit in Gurugram, Faridabad and Nuh as workers strike over privatisation
primary_source.content: Gurugram: A strike by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) workers plunged Gurugram, Faridabad, and Nuh districts into darkness since 10 pm on Wednesday, affecting thousands of consumers and industrial units.The power department received more than 3,000 complaints of outages within 12 hours of the strike, an official said on condition of anonymity on Thursday.The employees had announced the strike to protest against the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission's decision to grant a parallel electricity distribution licence to a private company for Gurugram and Nuh districts.Gurugram Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh held a meeting with the employees till late at night, urging them to reconsider their decision. However, the talks proved inconclusive, and no agreement was reached to end the strike.Several industrial units in Gurugram came to a standstill due to prolonged power cuts, with many owners complaining of potential losses running to crores of rupees.Deepak Maini, an industrialist and the chairman of the Progressive Federation of Trade and Industry, said there had been no power supply at Gurugram’s Sector-37 since 10 pm on Wednesday.Maini also expressed concern that any delay in the restoration of power supply could adversely affect production and business activities.He said that the availability of finished goods and the timely delivery of supplies could also be affected.“Power cuts at industrial units have brought machinery and production to a halt, impacting business operations. With operations suspended across hundreds of units, the risk of losses has increased,” Maini said.Apart from Gurugram, industrial units in Kadipur and Basai were also affected by power cuts.Ahmedabad Crime Branch catches MP man wanted in murder of six persons from GurugramSeveral residential colonies in Gurugram had to switch to generators as inverter backups ran out, residents said.In many areas, the breakdown of the power supply led to a shortage of drinking water. Residents say they are managing using water stored in tanks but claim that it will last only a few hours."Electricity and water are both essential services. Where is the government? Residents are held hostage by DHBVN staff. There has been no power since 10 pm yesterday. Either the government should settle employees' demands or depute the Disaster Management team to restore the supply. Officers are also showing helplessness. In such a situation, how will we come up with a solution?” said Shiv Kumar Sharma, a resident.In Faridabad, people in the New Industrial Township-2 area hit the streets, demanding restoration of power supply. They said the power cut also impacted water supply.Upon hearing information of a road blockade, police arrived at the scene and pacified the protesters, following which they were dispersed.In Nuh district, the power outage severely affected life in several areas, including Punhana, Nagina, and Firozpur Jhirka.Despite several attempts, the Superintending Engineer of the Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN), Operation Circle Gurugram-I, could not be contacted.

primary_source.headline: Kolkata stampede: Chorbagan Durga Puja treasurer held over ‘pandal collapsing’ misleading announcement; total 9 arrested
primary_source.content: Kolkata: Two persons were arrested on Friday for allegedly causing chaos by announcing that a portion of the crowd-puller Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata was collapsing, leading to the death of 19 people in a stampede, police said.With this, the total number of arrests in the stampede case has risen to nine.One of the accused, Sanjib Raha, was detained from Nadia district on Thursday and later put under arrest, while the other, Kushal Majumdar, was held on Friday from the Girish Park area of the metropolis, said a senior officer of Kolkata Police."Both of them were making announcements at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on the evening of the first day of Durga Puja. They were identified by scanning CCTV footage. We arrested Majumdar this morning and took him to our headquarters for questioning. If needed, we may interrogate them together," the officer told PTI.Three months too short to submit Chorbagan stampede probe report, will strive to meet deadline: SIT headAccording to police, Sanjib Raha was also the treasurer of the Chorbagan Durga Puja committee. Both Raha and Majumdar are residents of Kolkata's Amar Basu Sarani, just 50 metres from the puja spot.Raha has been charged under non-bailable sections of the BNS and will be produced in court later in the day, the police officer said."We are still piecing together the course of events that led to the stampede. One of the CCTV footage showed the two persons making announcements. They were heard warning revellers that the pandal was collapsing and asking visitors to leave the place immediately. It appeared that the announcements triggered panic and a rush towards the exit point," he said.According to the police officer, Raha was absconding since the October 17 incident and had switched off his mobile phone. Investigators tracked eight suspected mobile numbers to trace the accused as he was trying to contact family and friends using different numbers, he added.The government has formed a six-member special investigation team in consultation with the Calcutta High Court to probe the cause of the stampede and recommend measures to prevent such incidents in future.

primary_source.headline: CM Satheesan offers to host Raihan Vadra's exhibition in Keralam; BJP reacts
primary_source.content:
Keralam Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Thursday offered to host the exhibition of artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, in the state, amid controversy over the removal of his photographs depicting Delhi protests from Bikaner House in Delhi."Keralam would be happy and proud to host Raihan Vadra's No Idea Is Final exhibition in its entirety. No exclusions, no exceptions," Satheesan said in a post on 'X' on Thursday, tagging Raihan Vadra and Priyanka Gandhi.Kerala would be happy and proud to host Raihan Vadra’s No Idea Is Final exhibition in its entirety. No exclusions, no exceptions.
@priyankagandhi 
@raihanrvadra&mdash; V D Satheesan (@vdsatheesan) October 22, 2026
 Reacting to the CMs invite, Keralam BJP State President Rajeev Chandrasekhar, drew comparisons of how real Malayalee youth are teargassed, gas grenaded, violently assaulted by the Police at CMs instructions when they peacefully protest meanwhile preferential treatment is given to this youngster. He questioned the CM and asked if democracy and rights matter only when its the Dynast family. I hv no problms with CM @vdsatheesan inviting any exhibition to Keralam even Wayanad MPs son.

But what is wrong is this - The preferential treatment to this youngster - even as other real Malayalee youth are teargassed, gas grenaded, violently assaulted by Police at CMs instructions when they peacefully protest. 
What about their rights ? 
What about the rights of Keralams youth struggling with joblessness and political corruption ? What about the rights of the underage minor muslim girl being forced to be married in violation of POCSO ?

So the question to Congress in general, @RahulGandhi and @vdsatheesan in particular - Do democracy and rights matter only when its the Dynast n family and to no one else ? #APAKADAMPolitics

This is what is so egregious about @RahulGandhi’ s politics . 

This is why I say that he is a fraud and his entire politics is built on dishonesty, lies, corruption, anarchy and fraud.

#TruthAboutCorruptCongress
#CongressPoliticsOfLies&mdash; Rajeev Chandrasekhar  (@RajeevRC_X) October 23, 2026
  Raihan had his solo exhibition,' No Idea Is Final' lined up at Bikaner House in Delhi from October 22. He was told by the Bikaner House administration to pull down many of his pictures, including pictures of the national flag citing it as overtly political to showcase in the current political climate.He posted on Instagram stating how few hour before the show he was provided an ultimatum to remove the pictures and expressed his agony. "The show will go on in parts now" he mentioned in the post.         View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Raihan (@raihanrvadra)
 Raihan claimed  that the Bikaner House administration had warned him that the exhibition could be cancelled if he did not take down the pictures by 5 pm on Wednesday.As per media reports, the information reached him at 3:30 pm, and allotted him with 30 minutes to remove the photographs. His team put up blank frames in place of the works that were removed, which was also instructed to be taken down by the Bikaner House administration. Raihan said on Wednesday that he had shared the exhibition proposal and layout with the Bikaner House management well in advance. He also asserted that the photographs did not carry any political message but documented protests over the past six months.A visitor looks at the empty wall at Raihan Vadra's exhibition, at Bikaner House in New Delhi.Bikaner House released a press statement amid the ongoing controversy. "Certain photographs displayed as part of Mr. Raihan Vadra’s exhibition, “No Idea Is Final,” at Bikaner House was found to be inconsistent with the policy of the Bikaner House Management Society. Accordingly, their removal was requested," it said in the statement. "The photographs that are consistent with the Society’s policy have been continued to be displayed," it added.Priyanka had strongly criticised the move, saying that those in power who fear artistic expression end up losing the very power they seek to protect..@raihanrvadra 

When someone with power becomes afraid of the expression of another, he doesn’t know it, but he has already lost the very power he is trying to protect. 

You stand for what is true and everything beautiful will find its way to you. 

I am proud of you, always will be.

❤️ mama&mdash; Priyanka Gandhi Vadra (@priyankagandhi) October 22, 2026
 She slammed the removal of the photographs as ridiculous. The Congress MP accused the authorities of "muzzling" the voices of young people across the country.While a Bikaner House official said the administration was "not authorised to comment" on the matter, the BJP termed the allegations "fake news".When someone with power becomes afraid: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's veiled dig at govt over row surrounding son's exhibitionBJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari on Thursday said Bikaner House policy did not permit the display of political content and asked Priyanka Gandhi to find another way to "launch" her son into politics. (Inputs from PTI)

stories.primary_headline: Raye wins the Mercury Prize with This Music May Contain Hope

primary_source.headline: Raye wins the Mercury Prize with This Music May Contain Hope
primary_source.content: Raye is the 35th winner of the Mercury Prize, which was established to recognise albums that push the boundaries of music A pop record sprinkled with golden age Hollywood glamour, it beat the likes of Sir Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Jade to scoop the £25,000 prize. "I couldn't tell you how grateful I am to be holding this," said Raye, clutching her trophy at Newcastle's Utilita Arena. "I'm shaking, I'm jet-lagged, I'm tired. It's all blurry." It is the first time a pop album has won the coveted prize - which recognises the best British or Irish album of the last 12 months - since M People's Elegant Slumming in 1994. Speaking to the BBC afterwards, Raye said she'd "poured everything I had" into the record, which features the global hit song Where Is My Husband? "I made this album not focusing on commercial [success], not focusing on making things cookie-cutter," said the 28-year-old.

Her victory underscores a critical shift in the Mercury Prize's recognition criteria, celebrating an album Raye described as non-commercial and deeply personal, featuring the global hit "Where Is My Husband?". stories.primary_headline: No dilution in prescribed standards: NMC on denotification of medical education regulations

primary_source.headline: No dilution in prescribed standards: NMC on denotification of medical education regulations
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The National Medical Commission has asserted that the de-notification of the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 will not dilute prescribed standards of medical education and is intended to remove overlapping procedures.The Commission, which is the statutory body for medical education in the country, had on October 14 denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations (MSMER-2023).The denotification "does not, in any manner, dilute the prescribed standards of medical education or the regulatory oversight exercised by NMC," a statement by the Commission said.NMC grants one-time extra attempt to eligible MBBS students to clear first-year examNMC adds 13,636 MBBS seats for 2026-27, nearly 79% in private collegesUnder the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, the Undergraduate Medical Education Board (UGMEB) and Postgraduate Medical Education Board (PGMEB) are primarily entrusted with prescribing academic standards, minimum requirements and educational norms.The Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB), under Section 26 of the Act is specifically empowered to assess and inspect medical institutions, verify compliance with prescribed standards and initiate appropriate regulatory measures against institutions found deficient, it stated.The regulations had introduced a parallel mechanism of institutional evaluation, annual renewal and enforcement through UGMEB and PGMEB, resulting in overlapping regulatory functions, the statement said.Following judicial observations and a detailed examination of the statutory framework, the Commission decided to remove this duplication and align regulatory responsibilities with the provisions of the NMC Act, it stated.The requirement of Annual Disclosure Reports (ADR) remains mandatory and medical colleges will continue to submit annual disclosures concerning faculty, infrastructure, clinical facilities, patient load and other prescribed parameters, it emphasised.These disclosures remain available for scrutiny and verification through the statutory assessment and inspection mechanisms of MARB. Therefore, any suggestion that annual disclosures would become merely unverified claims is misplaced, the statement said.Further, all existing minimum standard requirements relating to faculty, infrastructure, clinical material, teaching facilities, attendance and academic standards will remain fully applicable.The MARB retains its statutory authority to conduct assessments and inspections, including where necessary without prior notice, and to take appropriate action against non-compliant institutions under the NMC Act and Regulation of the Establishment of Medical Institutions, Assessment and Rating Regulations, 2023, the statement said.The de-notification also safeguards actions already taken, liabilities incurred and proceedings initiated under MSMER-2023. The decision neither provides immunity for past violations nor exempts medical colleges from future regulatory action, it stressed.The only procedural change is the removal of the additional annual renewal requirement under MSMER-2023.Medical colleges remain subject to mandatory annual disclosures, prescribed minimum standards, institutional assessment and statutory enforcement."NMC remains committed to maintaining the highest standards of medical education while ensuring that regulation is transparent, effective and free from unnecessary duplication. Regulatory simplification must not be mistaken for regulatory relaxation," it stated."The NMC has removed an overlapping process, not the safeguards that protect the quality of medical education," the statement added.

primary_source.content: Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav said the Centre and state are jointly accelerating Madhya Pradesh’s development through major industrial and infrastructure initiatives. He said addressing the Viksit Bharat Industry and Trade Summit in Bhopal, that investment proposals worth ₹12 lakh crore had been translated into projects on the ground over the past two-and-a-half years, while entrepreneurs at the summit proposed fresh investments worth ₹7,500 crore.Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said that investment proposals worth ₹12 lakh crore had been translated into projects on the ground in the state over the past two-and-a-half years. Madhya Pradesh is strengthening its position across sectors, and transparent policies have made it easier for investors to establish industries. Investment promotion programmes and activities are being organised regularly to generate employment for the youth.Industry Brings Prosperity to PeopleChief Minister Dr. Yadav said that entrepreneurs contribute to improving people’s lives through investment across sectors. Their efforts in trade and industry sustain the livelihoods of millions of families. He also commended the industry’s active role in advancing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Make in India vision.Global Recognition for IndiaChief Minister Dr. Yadav said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, major countries around the world have begun viewing India with greater respect. He emphasised that Madhya Pradesh has considerable potential and that greater focus is needed on economic prosperity alongside agricultural development.Other States Adopting Madhya Pradesh’s Industrial ModelChief Minister Dr. Yadav said that Bhopal is hosting the Global Investors Summit for the second time, reflecting the state’s efforts to create an industry-friendly environment. The Regional Industry Conclave model developed by Madhya Pradesh has been appreciated by other states, several of which are adopting it. He said the Bhoomi Poojan performed earlier by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for the ₹50,000-crore downstream petrochemical unit at Bina Refinery would enable production of more than 2.2 million tonnes of petrochemical products annually in the coming years. These developments will accelerate growth not only in Madhya Pradesh but across the country.Chief Minister Dr. Yadav also released several publications brought out by the Federation. MSME Minister Shri Chaitanya Kashyap said the Chief Minister had helped create a favourable environment for investment in Madhya Pradesh. stories.primary_headline: Shovel Dance Collective: Everything in Readiness review – ecstatic, dissonant folk music fighting for sonic and spiritual freedom

primary_source.headline: Shovel Dance Collective: Everything in Readiness review – ecstatic, dissonant folk music fighting for sonic and spiritual freedom
primary_source.content: (tak:til)The nine-piece London-based group take a radically fresh approach to traditional music, sounding raging, lo-fi and joyful as they link Britain’s violent past to its presentThose thus far unaware of Shovel Dance Collective’s bracing approach to folk should probably note that their third album is not much interested in breaking newcomers in gently. Everything in Readiness kicks off with a three-song suite that lasts more than 10 minutes and takes you, via a series of dramatic sonic jump-cuts, from a grinding one-note drone to a reel that seems to split the difference between trad folk fiddle-playing and the punishing squall of the Velvet Underground’s Black Angel’s Death Song. It then leaps to Tally Ho! Hark Away!, which sets a hunting song first collected in the late 1940s over a blast of what might best be described as ecstatic noise. It’s genuinely hard to work out what instruments are involved in the clattering arrhythmic chaos behind the vocal – there’s definitely a heavily distorted guitar in the mix – but the effect is weirdly euphoric rather than claustrophobic: a kind of purgative release after the mounting weirdness of the preceding reel.If you’re looking for evidence that the nine-piece London-based group take a radically fresh approach to folk music, then there it is. The glib shorthand is that they’re doing for traditional English music what Lankum have done for its Irish equivalent – joining the dots with the kind of out-there experimentation that fills the pages of the Wire magazine – although it should be pointed out they sound almost nothing like Lankum. Anyone who already has an interest in leftfield explorations of British musical history might suggest their chaotic collage approach feels more akin to the fascinating collections of field recordings, folk song and avant garde composition released by Todmorden-based label Folklore Tapes. The music on Everything in Readiness careens unpredictably from gentle lo-fi recordings caked in distortion and tape hiss to the tumultuous, surging racket they serve up on their version of the traditional coalminer’s song Jowl, Jowl and Listen; from singing unaccompanied by anything but the sound of birdsong to the disquieting ambient shimmer of Who Killed Cock Robin? A Summoning (Kind Morning in our Fists), which sounds like it was recorded in a vast, echoing crypt. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: SBI customers’ data leak: Here’s how to protect yourself from phishing attacks
primary_source.content: Earlier this week, a report emerged that the customer database server of the State Bank of India was breached. And, customer data was being sold on darknet for the highest bidder.The exposed information includes account owners' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers (customer information file number), lead IDs (unique reference number generated to track a potential customer), and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files. Cut the call and verify directly at your nearest bank branch.2Secure your login credentialsRegularly update your netbanking passwords across both web and mobile applications to prevent unauthorized access.3Avoid suspicious links and APKsNever click on URL links or install APK files shared via WhatsApp, messengers, or social media, as they frequently contain malware.4Download apps from official storesEnsure you only install applications from recognized platforms like the Google Play Store, Apple App Store, or Microsoft Windows Store after checking user reviews.5Keep devices updated and protectedMaintain fully updated operating systems with the latest security patches and install reputable anti-virus software to defend against cyber threats.Key statistics4,000Reported affected accounts99 per centRisk rate of unverified APK files1930Emergency fraud helplineOne hourTime limit to report fraud for best recovery chanceProcessed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.Though it claims there is leakage of customer data of close to 4,000 accounts, the exposure seems much bigger.And, SBI's customers are still at risk of getting scammed online, particularly through frauds like phishing attacks and digital arrest.Google rolls out new AI-powered security features to Chrome to curb online fraudIt should be noted that the highest bidder on the darknet may now have thousands of customers' data with personally identifiable credentials. With that, they disguise themselves as a bank executive, CBI officer, an Income Tax official or a Supreme Court/High Court judge, and will surely make calls to customers of the leaked data.Here are tips on how to safeguard yourself from online scams like phishing and digital arrests:1) Whenever you receive a call from a person identifying themselves as a police or Income Tax official, a cellular company executive or a bank official stating that your account may get seized, never panic. Just tell them, I will speak to a bank official and just cut the call. Go to the nearest bank branch and clear the doubt.2) Regularly change the password of your netbanking account, both on the website and on the phone app.3)  If you ever receive messages with URL links to third-party app stores or APK files resembling a bank app, ignore them. Never install an APK file shared on WhatsApp or any messenger or social media platform. stories.primary_headline: Mecca Pact, Türkiye, and India’s West Asian challenge

primary_source.headline: Mecca Pact, Türkiye, and India’s West Asian challenge
primary_source.content: The submission of the ‘Mecca Pact’, a mutual defence agreement among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Türkiye, to the Grand National Assembly in Ankara on October 20 has triggered considerable excitement in India, with the focus primarily on the agreement’s hitherto secret text.Excessively or solely focusing on the agreement’s contents, compelling though it may be, is to miss the woods for the trees. Türkiye’s decision to submit the pact’s text for ratification by parliament has meant that its government has decided to incorporate the pact into its foreign and security architecture, nearly three months after its signature.It would be a mistake to see the Mecca Pact as some sort of a knee-jerk reaction to Houthi militia hostilities against Saudi Arabia, Iran’s missile and drone attacks against the Gulf states, or even the joint US-Israel attacks on Iran. The three parties to the August 7 agreement are all tired of non-State actors setting the agenda for West and South Asia, including the Gulf. The ascendancy of non-State actors became the rule, rather than the exception, since the rise of Afghanistan’s Taliban, the United States attack on Iraq in 2003, and the Arab Spring seven years later.Saudi Arabia rarely — if ever — walks into any security trap. It broods over and quietly considers for years before taking decisions on matters of foreign and security policies. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s decision to join the Mecca Pact signals the Kingdom’s desire for an inter-state and institutionalised security architecture for West Asia. This, after the crown prince’s preceding generation in the Al Saud royal family meddled for decades in regional disputes and hostilities, which created non-State actors like the anti-Soviet Mujahideen. Mohammed bin Salman wants to break from history.Pakistan defence expert stresses need to resolve disputes with IndiaPakistan, most of all, wants to escape from non-State actors, who have been running multiple parallel states within Pakistan. The Gulf countries have been advising Islamabad to get out of its self-perpetuating domestic violence and concentrate, instead, on economic development. This will save the Arab sheikhdoms from having to bail out Pakistan from time to time and salvage its fragile economy. The Pakistan Army’s current leadership — unlike Field Marshal Asim Munir’s predecessors — views the Mecca Pact as an opportunity to transcend South Asia’s fratricidal politics and emerge as a factor of stability in the Gulf. Pakistan’s recent mediation between Iran and the US did not occur in a vacuum. The Mecca Pact is a logical corollary.If this happens, it could end both the prolonged impasse in India-Pakistan ties and the regional deadlock in many matters involving all of South Asia. Any expansion of Pakistan’s security compass to cover West Asia — but primarily the Gulf — would arguably make it possible for India to lean on the Arab sheikhdoms and Iran to pressure Islamabad to reduce cross-border terrorism. Ending such terrorism altogether is easier said than done. Just as any rapprochement with Pakistan would not be popular with the Indian masses. A tough Pakistan policy gets votes. Even the Opposition is not supportive of any compromise with Islamabad.One thing is clear. India can no longer remain a mere passenger on a boat for plurilateral regional defence as it rapidly sails along the vast coastline of the Arabian Sea. Note the four-nation memorandum of understanding (MoU) named ‘Badr’ in Doha on October 21 to facilitate defence industry co-operation. Or the 14-nation Multinational Maritime Defense Coalition (MMDC) announced on July 30 to ensure freedom of navigation along the energy-vital waterways surrounding the Arabian Peninsula. India’s glaring omission from the MMDC does not augur well, especially because its neighbours — Bangladesh, the Maldives, and Pakistan — are its members. New Delhi can pretend that all this does not matter because India is an emerging global power. But how can India rise as a global power when it is systematically being diminished in its immediate as well as extended neighbourhood.Pakistan, Maldives sign 20 MoUs, including in defence, maritime securityThese are signals that the operationalisation of the Mecca Pact is not an event in isolation. An important course correction in New Delhi demands mending fences with Türkiye. Ankara already has 3,000 troops permanently stationed in Qatar. It has put in place institutional defence co-operation, including training and arms exports, with Syria, Libya, and Iraq.Like Türkiye during Operation Sindoor, Iran extended military assistance to Pakistan during its 1965 war with India and diplomatic support during the 1971 fight for Bangladesh. That did not prevent prime ministers Indira Gandhi and P V Narasimha Rao from extending the hand of friendship to Tehran. Rao, in particular, turned Iran from a foe into a friend. That is now the way to go with Türkiye too.K P Nayar has extensively covered West Asia and reported from Washington as a foreign correspondent for 15 years.(Disclaimer: The views expressed above are the author's own. They do not necessarily reflect the views of DH.)

primary_source.headline: Google rolls out new AI-powered security features to Chrome to curb online fraud
primary_source.content: In 2025, Google introduced on-device Gemini AI integration with Chrome to provide Enhanced Protection. It offered an additional, real-time layer of defence against tech support scams. This feature proved successful in combating this category of scam and helped prove the viability of LLM (Large Language Model)-assisted detection. Quick summary - click for full detailsConcise summary of key highlightsGoogle rolls out new security features to Chrome to curb online fraudIn one lineGoogle is enhancing Chrome's security with server-side Gemini AI to detect advanced online fraud and new HTTP warnings.Key highlights• Gemini AI Fraud DetectionGoogle is upgrading Chrome's security with a powerful server-side Gemini model to detect complex threats like fake antivirus and browser update scams.• Insecure HTTP WarningsChrome will now warn users when they visit legacy HTTP sites, alerting them to potential risks before they proceed.• Critical Security PatchesNew patches fix browser vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to steal personal information, with bug details restricted until updates are widely installed.Key statistics2025Introduction year of on-device Gemini AI integrationTwo weeksHTTP warning snooze duration156.0.8078.47/.48Windows and Mac Chrome version156.0.8078.47Linux Chrome versionProcessed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.Now, the search engine giant is improving its AI-powered security feature with a more powerful server-side Gemini model. It will be able to detect a broader range of threats, such as fake antivirus and browser update scams.Google rolls out next-gen Gemini 4 Argon AI model to developers globallyThis new feature can intuitively review webpage content to analyse key indicators, such as the brand represented, the page's intent, and a scam-likeliness score, giving Google the threat data it needs to identify deceptive sites. Safe Browsing considers Gemini's analysis, in combination with domain reputation and other security signals, to generate a final verdict on whether a particular website is safe or not.It will show a full-page red interstitial warning to users when a site is known to be malicious, and there is a high risk of user harm.Chrome gets new Gemini AI-powered security features.Also, as HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) adoption is not universal, some users need to regularly access some HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) sites of legacy brands. The latter are not secure, and they expose Chrome users to risks of malware, phishing, eavesdropping, and other threats to their private data. So, whenever a user goes to a website with just 'http', they will be warned that the particular website is insecure and asked to recheck if the user really wants to continue navigating on that website.Once the HTTP use is approved, Chrome will not warn again, unless the user has not visited the site for at least two weeks.Also, Google has rolled out new security patches to the Chrome browser. It fixes vulnerabilities in the browser that may allow hackers to steal personal information on devices.Access to bug details and links has been restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix. This way, Google avoids releasing security issues to criminals, who might target people who are late to update their Chrome app.Here's how to update to the latest version of Chrome on your computer:Go to the Chrome menu (three dots), select 'Help', then 'About Google Chrome', and Chrome will automatically check for updates and install them. Ensure your Chrome browser is updated to the latest versions-- 156.0.8078.47/.48 for Windows and Mac and 156.0.8078.47 for Linux.Google announces new Gemini AI-powered anti-fraud features for Android phonesGet the latest news on new launches, gadget reviews, apps, cybersecurity, and more on personal technology only on DH Tech.

sources.headline: Google rolls out new AI-powered security features to Chrome to curb online fraud

brief_bullets: Google has significantly upgraded Chrome’s security infrastructure by integrating a server-side Gemini AI model designed to identify sophisticated online fraud, including fake antivirus and browser update scams. By analyzing webpage content for deceptive intent and brand impersonation, this system enhances Google’s Safe Browsing protocols to provide real-time, full-page warnings against malicious sites. Additionally, Chrome now mandates explicit user acknowledgement for legacy HTTP connections, mitigating risks associated with unencrypted traffic. These updates, complemented by critical vulnerability patches, represent a strategic shift toward proactive, AI-driven threat detection. This evolution marks a transition from static blocklists to dynamic, context-aware security, effectively hardening the browser against increasingly complex social engineering tactics while simultaneously forcing a broader industry migration toward secure, encrypted web standards.
why_it_matters_bullets: AI-driven detection shifts the cybersecurity paradigm from reactive filtering to proactive, context-aware defense against sophisticated social engineering threats.

stories.primary_headline: RSS Chief’s Dussehra Delusions | Foreign conspiracies without evidence, foreign funds without scrutiny

primary_source.headline: RSS Chief’s Dussehra Delusions | Foreign conspiracies without evidence, foreign funds without scrutiny
primary_source.content: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Chief Mohan Bhagwat alleged that “demonic forces” from the West were trying to “destabilise India” in his annual Dussehra speech to the organisation. He also claimed that “regime change will not happen” in India like in France (sic), Albania, Bangladesh, or Nepal.Like the Narendra Modi government at the Centre, Bhagwat offered neither evidence of foreign interference nor of a conspiracy to force regime change.On the other hand, there is no dearth of evidence of both RSS-affiliated organisations and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi receiving support from foreign donors.The latest evidence comes from a US publication, Bellingcat. It shows that US donor-advised funds channelled millions of dollars in grants to RSS-affiliated NGOs in India. Donor-advised funds are a US charity-giving arrangement — individuals contribute money or assets to a charity they want to sponsor through these funds, receive a tax deduction, and can remain anonymous.'Regime change won't happen in India': RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on 'storm blowing in from West' opposing order and propriety  The investigation by Bellingcat, published on October 6, shows that two US-based charities, Ekal Vidyalaya Foundation of USA (Ekal USA), and Sewa International (Sewa USA), received $24.4 million from organisations managing donor-advised funds between 2020 and 2024. Together they received contributions and grants of $117.8 million. The ultimate donors remain anonymous, and are not part of the public records.Both Ekal USA and Sewa USA have close links with the RSS. Ekal USA began as a programme of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad of America. In India, Ekal Vidyalaya schools have been criticised for indoctrinating poor children with Hindutva ideology. The Sewa USA website also points to its RSS connections and describes Seva Bharathi in India, an RSS-sponsored group, as its sister organisation.The investigation found that both were funding sister organisations, also affiliated to the RSS in India. The Ekal Vidyalaya project — an RSS affiliate — received $33.7 million in foreign grants from Ekal USA. Similarly, Sewa USA reported giving foreign grants to India and South Asia amounting to $29.7 million. It is not known how much was given to its sister organisation in India, Seva Bharathi, during this period (2020-2024).Both Ekal Vidyalaya Foundation of India and Seva Bharathi have FCRA clearance from an RSS-friendly Modi government. Logically, however, merely on the basis of these organisations receiving foreign funding, can it be said that either they or their parent organisation, the RSS, have automatically become agents of foreign powers?How is it then that the RSS readily accuses those who challenge the Modi government as operating under foreign influence (having not even provided evidence of foreign funding), while financial and ideological networks located abroad who fund its associates in India are considered beyond suspicion.The same standard should be applied equally to both those who are critical of the government and those ideologically aligned to it. It should include full disclosure of funding, transparency about the organisational relationships with the funding agencies abroad, disclosure of the purpose of the expenditure, and production of evidence of any improper influence.As for the Modi government, rallies abroad, at Madison Square Garden in New York, Wembley Stadium in London, or ‘Howdy, Modi!’ in Houston — are foreign-funded events and a form of transnational political interference because of how they impact domestic politics in India. Through these events, foreign citizens, albeit of Indian origin (PIOs), pool millions of dollars that indirectly influence Indian elections and the domestic political atmosphere through image-boosting campaigns for Modi.These events also interfere in the domestic politics of the host country, such as in Modi’s partisan sloganeering for local political leaders, as in ‘Abki baar, Trump Sarkar’. The events also turn Indian community organisations in the host country into a lobby, to press Western political leaders, as in pressing them to overlook human rights or democratic backsliding within India.So, neither Bhagwat nor the Modi government have a leg to stand on when they talk of foreign forces interfering in Indian domestic politics.Bhagwat’s second proposition in his Dussehra speech was that it is a “wrong perception that problems get solved only through agitation”.Of course, problems also get resolved through dialogue, negotiation, and parliamentary debate. However, when people feel that these methods have failed repeatedly to make those in power listen — as in the case of voter exclusion through SIR — are citizens not free to force negotiation with the State through peaceful resistance in the indigenous manner blessed by Mahatma Gandhi?'Communist-Islamist cabal' running protest industry to undermine Brand Bharat, says RSS-linked magazine Organiser Bhagwat’s statement that “regime change won’t happen in India” is wishful and inaccurate. Sudden upheavals may be harder in India because of its size and established institutions, but they are not impossible. India’s history is replete with examples where mass agitations forced the removal of chief ministers (Chimanbhai Patel’s ouster in 1974), contributed to the electoral defeat of governments (the J P Movement in 1974-1975), made governments reverse policy (farmers’ movement in 2020-2021) and altered the balance of power in Parliament (fall of the Morarji Desai government in 1979 after the disintegration of the Janata Dal).The fall of a government does not mean a collapse of the political system. Hypothetically, the Modi government could fall if the National Democratic Alliance coalition breaks down, or if a mass movement leads to an early general election.Bhagwat has conflated a number of contemporary examples of protest to create a scary picture of political anarchy worldwide waiting to overwhelm India. In truth they are all different. The French government of Michel Bernier fell in 2024 after losing a vote of confidence — through a constitutional parliamentary process without an overthrow of the French State. The current protests in France by students and labour unions have not led to the fall of the French government either. The ongoing protests in Albania demonstrate the government of Prime Minister Edi Rama is under pressure, but it has not yet fallen.Bangladesh and Nepal demonstrate a quite different pathway where political channels had become ineffective or inaccessible and the State’s political institutions lost their capacity to negotiate with the mass movement. It is reasonable to think that based on India’s size, its federal structure, its strong institutions, and military traditions that will not be the trajectory of Indian politics today.With the long tradition and maturity of mass movements in India, the government and the RSS chief ought to take a lesson from that history instead of branding the demand for rethinking current policy changes in the electoral system as a foreign conspiracy.Bharat Bhushan is a New Delhi-based journalist.(Disclaimer: The views expressed above are the author's own. They do not necessarily reflect the views of DH.)

stories.primary_headline: Quote of the day by Wole Soyinka: “When is playacting rebuked by reality…”

primary_source.headline: Quote of the day by Wole Soyinka: “When is playacting rebuked by reality…”
primary_source.content: “When is playacting rebuked by reality? When is fictionalizing presumptuous?”Explanation: Can art truly capture the brutality of real life, or does representing suffering on a stage risk turning it into a spectacle for an audience? Nigerian playwright and Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka raised these questions while reflecting on the limits of artistic expression and the responsibility of writers to confront uncomfortable truths.“When is playacting rebuked by reality? When is fictionalizing presumptuous?” Soyinka asked in his Nobel Lecture, This Past Must Address Its Present, delivered on December 8, 1986. He followed these questions with another: “What happens after playacting?”The questions emerged from Soyinka’s own experience as a young playwright and performer. In 1958, he participated in an experimental theatre production in London titled Eleven Men Dead at Hola, which examined the deaths of 11 Kenyan detainees at Hola Camp during British colonial rule.Quote of the day by Salman Rushdie: “For literature to exist, there must be freedom.”The production dramatised the violence inflicted on the detainees and contrasted it with the official account, which claimed they had died after drinking poisoned water. Soyinka had been assigned the role of a camp guard but refused to perform in the scene, troubled by the way the staging represented the brutality it sought to expose.In his Nobel Lecture, he explained that the theatrical presentation seemed inadequate to the horror of the actual events. He questioned whether dramatising suffering could provoke meaningful change or instead allow audiences to experience a sense of sympathy without confronting the reality behind it.About Wole Soyinka: Wole Soyinka is a Nigerian playwright, poet, novelist and essayist known for his engagement with political power, colonialism, human rights and social injustice.Soyinka was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986, becoming the first African writer to receive the honour.&nbsp;

primary_source.headline: Prepare for supply chain disruption from cyber or climate emergencies, Streeting warns public
primary_source.content: Wes Streeting warned people needed to be more aware of emerging risks facing the UK and make plans to deal with them. He added that the government was launching a "national resilience conversation" to raise awareness, including advice for households like stocking up on food, bottled water and first aid supplies. Streeting told BBC One's Question Time that the UK is facing a greater threat to the country, "than we have certainly for most, if not all, of my lifetime". Speaking to an audience at the UK Gun Hall Plant in Telford earlier on Thursday, where it was announced production of tank gun barrels would return to the UK, he spoke of "everyday challenges" facing households. Streeting said the public need to be prepared for "increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks" on businesses, or supply chain disruption caused by "hostile state actors or terrorists". The defence secretary referenced the critical security flaw in the PHP programming language which has left organisations around the world scrambling to update their systems.

primary_source.headline: The Guardian view on AI safety: the push for global regulation must advance | Editorial
primary_source.content: The current US administration is an obstacle, but public demand for protection will ultimately prevailOrganisations around the world scrambled on Thursday to fix critical flaws in PHP, the software that powers much of the web. The vulnerabilities could allow attackers to take control of affected servers. Some websites were taken offline as a precaution while fixes were installed. The paradox is that while AI helped researchers uncover the flaw, it also threatens to accelerate the ability to exploit it. Amazon said that it had detected an attempt before the public disclosure of the PHP flaws.What the episode highlights is AI’s central role in security – and not always for the right reasons. OpenAI’s models have also been responsible for two alarming hacks this year – a security breach of an Australian health department website and a raid by a swarm of AI bots on Hugging Face, an AI services platform. Citing those incidents, the AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, warned that a similar cyber-attack on the UK is “likely, if not inevitable”. Continue reading...

sources.headline: The Guardian view on AI safety: the push for global regulation must advance | Editorial

brief_bullets: Global cybersecurity infrastructure faces mounting instability as critical vulnerabilities in PHP software, which powers a significant portion of the internet, were recently exposed. While AI tools assisted researchers in identifying these flaws, the technology simultaneously empowers malicious actors to accelerate exploitation, as evidenced by recent breaches involving OpenAI models and automated bot swarms targeting platforms like Hugging Face. UK AI minister Kanishka Narayan has warned that such sophisticated cyber-attacks are increasingly inevitable, underscoring the urgent need for robust international regulatory frameworks. This incident highlights a dangerous paradox where the very tools designed to enhance digital security are being weaponized to compromise the foundational integrity of global web servers, necessitating immediate, coordinated defensive measures from both governments and private technology organizations.
why_it_matters_bullets: The dual-use nature of AI necessitates urgent global regulation to prevent systemic collapse of critical digital infrastructure.

stories.primary_headline: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

primary_source.headline: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
primary_source.content: Medics at el-Fasher's Saudi Hospital performed a Caesarean by phone light on the day it was bombed UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes. The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings. The health minister of the group's civilian-affiliated government dismissed the allegations as propaganda. Dr Alaa Eldin Nugud said it was a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation. Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times.

stories.primary_headline: Youth Should Dream Big and Use Their Success to Serve Society and the Nation: President Smt. Droupadi Murmu

primary_source.headline: Youth Should Dream Big and Use Their Success to Serve Society and the Nation: President Smt. Droupadi Murmu
primary_source.content: President Smt. Droupadi Murmu called upon young people to dream big, broaden their outlook and link their success to service to society and the nation. She said that circumstances and challenges may vary, but young people should have the desire to create something new, bring about improvements and establish their own identity. The country’s progress would gain further momentum when the individual efforts of young people are aligned with collective and national goals.The President was addressing the ‘Seva Samman Parv and Yuva Prabodhan’ programme organised on the occasion of Nuakhai at Sardar Balbir Singh Juneja Indoor Stadium in Raipur. Governor Shri Ramen Deka, Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai and a large number of young people, women and people from various sections of society attended the programme.Extending Nuakhai greetings, President Smt. Murmu said that Nuakhai Milan is more than a cultural gathering; it is a celebration of our rich traditions, mutual harmony and social unity. Such events provide an opportunity to remain connected to our roots, take pride in our cultural heritage and pass on Indian values to future generations.She said that Nuakhai is a festival that preserves our agricultural traditions, expresses gratitude to nature and strengthens the spirit of community. Food is more than a means of satisfying hunger; it symbolises the hard work of farmers, the generosity of the earth and nature’s priceless gifts. Respecting food, recognising farmers’ contribution and protecting natural resources are our collective responsibility.Young People Should Combine Knowledge with Humility, Ambition with Ethics and Success with a Spirit of ServicePresident Smt. Murmu urged young people never to stop learning. She encouraged them to read books, ask questions, understand new things and continuously develop their knowledge and skills. She asked them to set goals and face challenges with courage. Success and failure are part of life, she said, adding that instead of becoming discouraged by failure, young people should learn from it, improve themselves and move forward.She said that young people should combine knowledge with humility, ambition with ethics and success with a spirit of service. An achievement becomes truly meaningful when one’s knowledge helps someone in need, one’s talent solves a problem and one’s success brings positive change to society.The President said that nation-building depends not only on major decisions but also on the small, honest efforts of crores of citizens. She urged every young person to carry out their work with honesty, dedication and sensitivity. These qualities would strengthen their contribution to realising the resolve of a developed India.Equal Participation of Women Essential for a Developed IndiaExpressing happiness over the participation of a large number of women in the programme, President Smt. Murmu said that women’s equal participation is essential to achieving the goal of making India a developed nation by 2047. The nation cannot progress to its full potential without empowering half its population.She called upon women to actively participate in work for the country and society. The President urged men, particularly young men, to provide their sisters and daughters with an environment and opportunities that allow them to realise their dreams without obstacles. Respect for women should be reflected not merely in words but also in our thinking, behaviour and daily conduct.Areas Once Gripped by Terror Are Now Witnessing DevelopmentReferring to the positive changes in Chhattisgarh, President Smt. Murmu expressed happiness that the efforts of the Central and State Governments, together with the determination of young people, were helping the state’s youth leaving misguided path of Naxalism and join the mainstream.She said that areas once gripped by terror are now witnessing development. This change is benefiting young people and their families while also accelerating the development of Chhattisgarh and India as a whole.Nuakhai Is a Festival of Social Unity and Service: Governor Shri Ramen DekaExtending Nuakhai Juhar greetings to the people of the state, Governor Shri Ramen Deka said that the festival celebrates the arrival of the new harvest while expressing gratitude to Mother Earth, honouring farmers’ hard work and bringing people together to share their happiness. It strengthens our rich agricultural culture, social unity and tradition of mutual cooperation.Describing President Smt. Droupadi Murmu’s presence as a matter of good fortune and an occasion of inspiration for the state, the Governor said that her struggles, simplicity, dedication and spirit of service inspire everyone. He called upon young people to make service a way of life, stay away from substance abuse and misguided paths, and contribute to nation-building through knowledge, skills and innovation.Governor Shri Deka said that healthy, educated young people with strong values and a spirit of service form the firm foundation of a strong society and a developed nation. Appreciating the blood donors, particularly women donors, he said that blood donation is one of the greatest services to humanity.President Smt. Droupadi Murmu’s Life Is an Inspiration for Daughters and Youth: Chief Minister Shri SaiChief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai warmly welcomed President Smt. Droupadi Murmu on behalf of the three crore people of Chhattisgarh. He said that the President shares a deep bond with Chhattisgarh and that the people of the state hold her in great respect and affection.Chief Minister Shri Sai said that President Smt. Murmu’s life is an inspiring example of struggle, simplicity, service, education and determination. Her journey from a small village in Odisha to the country’s highest constitutional office is a source of inspiration, particularly for the nation’s daughters, young people and those in tribal and rural areas. Her guidance would give the state’s youth fresh energy to set ambitious goals and contribute to nation-building.The Chief Minister said that Nuakhai celebrates our rich agricultural culture, welcomes the new harvest and expresses gratitude to Mother Earth. Chhattisgarh and Odisha share centuries-old social and cultural ties. The Odia community has made a significant contribution to Chhattisgarh’s development through its hard work, simplicity and spirit of service. Organising Seva Samman and Yuva Prabodhan on the auspicious occasion of Nuakhai is an important initiative linking cultural traditions with social service and support for young people.Youth at the Centre of Efforts to Build a Developed ChhattisgarhChief Minister Shri Sai said that young people would play a decisive role in realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s resolve to make India a developed nation by 2047. With youth at the centre of its efforts to build a developed Chhattisgarh, the State Government is expanding opportunities in education, employment, skill development, innovation and entrepreneurship.He said that five new medical colleges have been started in Geedam, Kunkuri, Janjgir-Champa, Manendragarh and Kawardha to expand medical education. A National Skill Training Institute is being established in Nava Raipur, where approximately 4,000 young people will receive training in modern technology and vocational skills every year. The Chhattisgarh State AI Mission aims to provide artificial intelligence training to six lakh students.The Chief Minister said that employment and entrepreneurship are being encouraged through the new industrial policy. A Rs. 100 crore startup fund has been created under the Chhattisgarh Startup Promotion Policy to support innovations by young people. Steps have also been taken towards establishing prestigious institutions in the state, including a forensic university campus, NIFT and NIELIT. A decision has been taken to provide 10 per cent reservation in direct recruitment for the posts of police constable, forest guard and prison warder to Agniveers from Chhattisgarh who complete four years of military service.He said that the State Government aims to provide every young person in the state with adequate opportunities to progress, so that their talent, energy and abilities contribute to building a developed Chhattisgarh.2,548 People Donate Blood at Raktadan MahakumbhCongratulating the blood donors who participated in the Raktadan Mahakumbh organised under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, Chief Minister Shri Sai said that blood donation is a great service to humanity. A total of 2,548 people, including 1,188 women, voluntarily donated blood during the campaign. He described it as an excellent example of Chhattisgarh’s spirit of service, community participation and Nari Shakti.Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Arun Sao and Shri Vijay Sharma, Union Minister of State Shri Tokhan Sahu, Health Minister Shri Shyam Bihari Jaiswal, Revenue Minister Shri Tank Ram Verma, Food Minister Shri Dayaldas Baghel, Technical Education Minister Shri Guru Khushwant Saheb, Rajya Sabha MP Smt. Laxmi Verma, MLA Shri Purandar Mishra, other public representatives and a large number of distinguished citizens were present on the occasion.

stories.primary_headline: Ban on patta for tanks: Supreme Court orders demolition of encroachments in Tiruvallur after allotting alternate site to flat owners

primary_source.headline: Ban on patta for tanks: Supreme Court orders demolition of encroachments in Tiruvallur after allotting alternate site to flat owners
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has upheld the absolute prohibition on granting ryotwari patta for communal tanks and ooranis and directed the Tamil Nadu government to allot a vacant, commensurate site to flat owners within six months and only thereafter demolish residential structures standing on 0.22 acres of a classified water body in Tiruvallur district.A bench of Justices S V N Bhatti and N V Anjaria dismissed civil appeals filed by flat buyer S Gururaj and others challenging Madras High Court orders that had ordered eviction of all occupants, demolition of unauthorised structures across 1.68 acres of Survey No. 572, and restoration of the water body. The apex court made it clear that Section 14-A of the Tamil Nadu Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, expressly bars the grant of ryotwari patta for private tanks or ooranis and requires cancellation of any such patta issued in error.Communal water bodies vest in the state free from all encumbrances and do not qualify as ryoti land eligible for patta, the bench held. Under Section 3(16) of the Act, ryoti land is defined as cultivable land in an estate other than private land, but expressly excludes beds and bunds of tanks, drainage channels and irrigation works. Consequently, land classified as communal water body poramboke cannot be converted into ryoti land or granted patta, the bench said.The court rejected arguments that the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority’s notification of the area as a “Mixed Residential Zone” had altered the character of the land. “A zoning designation does not efface the statutory classification of land as an objectionable watercourse poramboke,” the court observed, clarifying that zoning regulations cannot extinguish the government’s title over communal lands, forests or water bodies.Kerala PCC guards leaders against Oommen Chandy sentiments being dragged to attack V D SatheesanThe High Court had earlier found that the District Revenue Officer, Tiruvallur, had no authority to reclassify the communal poramboke and that the 2011 patta was a product of administrative fraud. It had directed the district administration to restore the water body within 16 weeks and ordered an inquiry, disciplinary action and criminal proceedings against the officials involved.The Supreme Court noted that municipal authorities had sanctioned building plans and that revenue records had been altered, leading bona fide purchasers to believe the land was free of objection. Directing immediate demolition without addressing the hardship of flat owners would cause irreparable injury, the bench said. It therefore ordered the Chief Secretary and the District Collector, Tiruvallur, to provide alternative land to the flat owners represented by their society, preferably within six months, and only then proceed with demolition of the constructed portion measuring 0.22 acres.Development work on the remaining vacant and unoccupied area may continue without hindrance, the court clarified. Flat owners and the appellant bank remain free to pursue civil remedies against the developer, landowner or mortgagor. The State is also free to initiate or conclude disciplinary proceedings against erring officials for failing to protect water bodies and maintain accurate records, the bench said.The 1948 Act abolished the permanent settlement system and introduced ryotwari settlement. It recognised a ryot’s right to patta only in respect of ryoti land and deliberately excluded tanks, channels and other lands set apart for common village use. Section 14-A created a prohibitory mechanism that renders any order granting patta for non-ryoti land void, the court noted. The District Revenue Officer’s action in the present case, the court held, went beyond the statutory scheme and could not be sustained.

stories.primary_headline: Surveillance and 'constant paranoia': Western diplomats tell BBC of life in war-time Moscow

primary_source.headline: Surveillance and 'constant paranoia': Western diplomats tell BBC of life in war-time Moscow
primary_source.content: Ex-US and French ambassadors Lynne Tracy and Pierre Lévy were among those to speak to the BBC of their time in Moscow US, UK and European diplomats once played a crucial role in Russia, defusing tensions even at the worst moments of the Cold War. But now, deemed "unfriendly" by President Vladimir Putin's government, Western ambassadors are under constant surveillance, isolated and increasingly cut off from the country they were sent to understand, as the war in Ukraine grinds on through its fifth year. The BBC has spoken to five diplomats who have served in Russia since it launched its full-scale invasion. Tracy's 30-year career took her to countries like Pakistan, where she survived an armed attack in 2008. But she says that even under constant physical threat, her posting in Peshawar was, in a sense, easier than Russia. "There, I still felt that there were things within my control. What made Moscow more difficult were the high levels of uncertainty."

stories.primary_headline: Leaked Mass Effect: Universe trailer gives a taste of what we're all missing

primary_source.headline: Leaked Mass Effect: Universe trailer gives a taste of what we're all missing
primary_source.content:
Those mourning yesterday's shuttering of highly praised and influential developer BioWare also had to deal with the cancellation of the next Mass Effect game, which was first teased back in 2020. Today, we got our best look at what that game could have been with a short, leaked trailer for Mass Effect: Universe.
In the roughly two-minute montage—which describes itself as "in-engine footage from our small team" that "uses our pre-production assets"—an ex-military officer wearing an N7 trenchcoat (similar to the one seen in that 2020 teaser) encounters an Asari at a bar. He talks of his frustration with military life—"by the time you put out one fire, another had already started"—before discussing his new line of work "stopping [the fires] before they start" and "making the choices no one else is willing to make. Going where others are afraid to go."
Mass Effect: Universe Trailer

stories.primary_headline: Loidis: From the Toolkit of Lovers review – epic 111-minute album is a teeming universe of detail

primary_source.headline: Loidis: From the Toolkit of Lovers review – epic 111-minute album is a teeming universe of detail
primary_source.content: (Incienso)Brian Leeds, AKA Huerco S, keeps raising the temperature on his once-chilly ambient on an ambitious record full of delightful detail and ASMR-inducing sound designThe sun barely seemed to rise in the earlier work of US electronic producer Brian Leeds. As Huerco S he put out the audio equivalent of 5pm November gloaming: lo-fi, low-lumen ambient and house music, flickering as if through a thicket of pine. But the light sharpened on his 2022 album Plonk, and for his project Loidis – on 2024 album One Day and this year’s stunning remix of James K’s Peel – the temperature seemed to rise along with the tempos. It wasn’t quite Balearic summer, but certainly Baltic spring or Adriatic autumn.His new album is his grandest statement across either project: 111 minutes of music across six sides of vinyl, a scale he goes a long way towards justifying. In tracks reminiscent of the microhouse sound of early 00s acts such as Luomo, the synth chords have Leeds’ trademark degraded shimmer, paired with ticklish snares and delightful ASMR-inducing sound design, stereo effects panning from right to left with quicksilver physicality. It’s hugely pleasurable to let your mind zoom in and out of these arrangements, marvelling at the microscopic detail then appreciating the overarching sense of groove, further enhanced by big melodic motifs: the playful echoing notes in TT Stunt, or the Afrobeat bassline of Running Rich. A couple of tracks in the second half lack the adventure elsewhere, but at least 90 of the minutes here are riveting, psychedelic even on nothing stronger than a cup of tea. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Must unite society against divisive forces; inspire citizens towards self-reliance: Prime Minister
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday called for efforts to address emerging societal ills and new challenges, unite society against divisive forces and inspire citizens towards self-reliance.Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan here, Modi said Chinmaya Mission was not merely an institution but a thought—Chinmaya, meaning pure consciousness—was founded by a Chinmaya sage, whose journey over the decades had also been marked by divine resolves."In the past decades, times have changed, new challenges have emerged before the country, and new societal ills have surfaced. Today, the responsibility of solving them rests upon all of us," Modi said.'Deafening silence, calibrated concessions': Congress slams PM Modi over face-offs with China in Arunachal Pradesh"We must unite society against the forces that seek to divide us. We must make our citizens aware and inspired towards self-reliance. We must connect every individual with the resolve of a Developed India by 2047. For these objectives, we must become even more proactive," he added.The prime minister said the nation was the birthplace of Indian culture and the foundation of the country's existence."Thanks to the efforts of Chinmaya Mission, today millions of youth are working as cultural brand ambassadors of India. These youth are carrying Indian values to the new generation," he said.The three-day event, being held from Friday, brings together over 9,000 participants from India and abroad.The event marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951 to make the wisdom of Vedanta and the Bhagavad Gita accessible to all.

primary_source.content: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracyLook, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus.According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Profitability no ground to stall insolvency process under IBC: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has ruled that a company’s profitability is neither a legally relevant factor nor a reliable indicator of its ability to service debt when deciding whether to initiate corporate insolvency resolution proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih held that the threshold for establishing default under Section 7 is a summary, prima facie one, to be assessed on the preponderance of probabilities from documentary evidence on record. The court clarified that what must be proved is the occurrence of default—a static historical event—and not a precise determination of the outstanding debt amount for admission of the petition.Insolvency law main factor in improving health of country's banking sector: FM in Lok SabhaDisputes over the exact quantum of debt do not negate the existence of default or prevent admission, provided the statutory threshold under Section 4 is met, the bench said. It emphasised the limited scope of inquiry at the admission stage.A record of default issued by an information utility ranks highest in the evidentiary hierarchy and creates a presumption of default that can be displaced only by clear, cogent and compelling material, the court underscored. Other documents such as loan agreements, account statements and balance confirmations form a second tier and may collectively establish default under the summary standard, the court added.The Code, the court noted, is premised on timely intervention upon the occurrence of default under Section 3(12), rather than waiting for commercial or balance-sheet insolvency. It rejected the argument that profitability measured by EBITDA precludes admission into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP).The October 15, 2026 ruling came in appeals filed by Deepak Raheja and another against a common August 19, 2025 judgment of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), Principal Bench, New Delhi. The NCLAT had upheld July 8, 2025 orders of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Mumbai Bench, admitting Section 7 petitions and initiating CIRP against GSTAAD Hotels Pvt Ltd and Neo Capricorn Plaza Pvt Ltd.The status of Omkara Assets Reconstruction Private Limited as a financial creditor stood conclusively established by an assignment agreement of December 27, 2022, whose validity had been upheld by the Karnataka High Court and affirmed by the Supreme Court. Finding that default above the Section 4 threshold was established on the record, and detecting no perversity in the concurrent findings of the NCLT and NCLAT, the court dismissed the appeals. It directed that the CIRP against both corporate debtors proceed in accordance with law.During the hearing, the court was told that a compilation of judgments placed on record by the appellants contained AI-generated non-existent citations. While the court initially proposed heavy costs, it deleted the costs order upon being informed of the death of the first appellant, stating “no order as to costs.”

stories.primary_headline: Imagine if, for once, Labour decided to tell the truth about immigration | Gaby Hinsliff

primary_source.headline: Imagine if, for once, Labour decided to tell the truth about immigration | Gaby Hinsliff
primary_source.content: Our economy needs it. The NHS needs it. And making foreign workers’ lives more miserable – as the home secretary plans to do – will undermine integrationMy mum’s carer was uncharacteristically late one morning. She didn’t want to say why at first, but it turned out she’d found her previous client – an elderly lady living all alone, with no family to visit – collapsed on the floor, barely alive. It was a lot to cope with for someone only in their early 20s, a reminder of the heavy responsibility this job carries. Watching the carers who helped both my parents in their respective final weeks taught me that while the work itself might seem mundane, the emotional and social skills needed to do it well – to coax some sense out of the confused, to jolly along the lonely, and to soothe the dying, to walk in and out of unfamiliar houses all day long without quite knowing what you might find – are anything but.Yet like so many jobs predominantly done by women, care has long been relentlessly undervalued. That means lousy pay, little public recognition, and now – at least for the disproportionately large chunk of this workforce who are migrant workers – the disorientating realisation that the government can snap its fingers and all your life plans are upended overnight.Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Uber rival inDrive eyes 2027 robotaxi tests in Central Asia with Pony.ai and Nvidia

primary_source.headline: Uber rival inDrive eyes 2027 robotaxi tests in Central Asia with Pony.ai and Nvidia
primary_source.content: The companies said Friday that they had signed a memorandum of understanding to explore bringing Pony.ai’s robotaxis to inDrive’s platform — a reflection of the growing interest in self-driving technology beyond the U.S. and China. Testing will begin in Kazakhstan’s capital, Astana, in the first half of 2027, inDrive CTO Yuri Misnik told TechCrunch. The tests will initially involve a safety operator, with fully driverless rides as the eventual goal. Under the proposed plan, Pony.ai would provide its Gen-7 robotaxis, which inDrive would offer through its ride-hailing app and operate in Kazakhstan. Nvidia, on the other hand, would supply the AI technology, including its Hyperion platform and Halos safety system. inDrive, which has built its business around affordable rides, is looking to bring a similar focus to autonomous ride-hailing as it explores a market where Uber and other rivals are already making moves. “Our approach is capital-light by design,” said Misnik. “We work with a range of partners in different markets, combining their expertise with ours to deliver a better customer experience.” Nvidia says its Hyperion platform could lower the cost of developing robotaxis by giving companies a ready-made foundation of sensors and computing technology, rather than requiring them to build and integrate everything themselves. The company also offers its Alpamayo model and tools to generate synthetic data and test autonomous driving systems across different driving scenarios.

That triggered years of health anxiety, with hours spent searching symptoms, feeling panicked and isolated. "I was constantly Googling and using ChatGPT, every source I could get that could tell me what was wrong," she says.

stories.primary_headline: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access

primary_source.headline: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
primary_source.content:
A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining "userland" access that he says "lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO."
The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4, the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called "tethered" hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access.
Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI's Codex to poke at SmileBasic's language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). After "substantial effort for ~2 weeks," that harness discovered a 32-bit integer overflow that occurs when removing items from an array in SmileBasic. That error gives access to an array pointer, which in turn allows read and write access to portions of system memory.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.

primary_source.headline: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.
primary_source.content:
NASA does not have, nor want, nuclear weapons. But when it comes to a particular metric that is part of the Artemis Program to land people on the Moon, NASA guards a particular number like they are trying to prevent outsiders from cracking nuclear codes.
I am speaking of the number of Starship launches required to fuel a Starship-based lunar lander in low-Earth orbit such that it can fly out to the Moon, land there, and return to lunar orbit.
This number has been a moving target over the years. The general response from NASA has typically been, 'We don't know for sure, so we're not going to say.' In 2023, for example, the then-director of NASA's Human Landing System, Lisa Watson-Morgan, told Ars, "We have a general idea, but I’m reluctant to say exactly what that is."Read full article
